plan: [ In a private-values, second-price auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Overbidding can make you win at a price above your value (negative payoff); underbidding can make you lose when you would have had positive surplus. With independent values and only 1 round, there’s no reputational or dynamic benefit to deviating. Given my value is $3.00 and bids are in $0.10 increments, I should bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit. ]

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values and rational opponents, the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Overbidding risks negative profit if the second-highest bid exceeds my value; underbidding only reduces my chance to win without lowering the payment when I do win. This is a single round, so no signaling is useful. With value 24 and 0.1 bid increments, I should bid exactly 24. Ties at 24 are resolved randomly; bidding above 24 is strictly dominated. ]

Second-price auction with independent private values: truthful bidding is weakly dominant. Overbidding risks paying above my value if I beat a higher-value rival; underbidding risks losing when I should profitably win. Rational opponents will also bid their values. With no history and one round, maximize expected profit by bidding exactly my value: 11.
